// Must-trip fixture reproducing the exact shapes this phase removed from the
// run-dir writers in internal/security and internal/quality, and from the
// red-proof repoint apply path.
//
// It is a FIXTURE rather than an assertion about the post-fix tree on purpose:
// those sites are clean now, so a scan calibrated on them proves only that it
// was written after the fix. This keeps the regression falsifiable when the
// tree moves.
package scanfixture

import (
	"os"
	"strings"

	"github.com/Rivil/dross/internal/pathfence"
)

// The security.go / quality.go report writer as it was: an unwrapped path
// handed straight to os.WriteFile.
func writeRunReport(reportPath pathfence.Contained, b *strings.Builder) error {
	return os.WriteFile(reportPath.String(), []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
}

// The findings ledger writer, before the seam took over.
func saveLedger(c pathfence.Contained, body []byte) error {
	return os.WriteFile(c.String(), body, 0o644)
}

// The red-proof repoint rollback write — the one call a partial adoption is
// most likely to leave behind, since every behavioural test passes without it.
func rollback(doc pathfence.Contained, orig []byte, mode os.FileMode) error {
	return os.WriteFile(doc.String(), orig, mode)
}
